intended_object: The canonical projection Z_i(K) → H_i(K), from the cycles in degree i of a homological complex onto its homology in degree i, which sends a cycle to its homology class. The docstring says this, and so do the name and the module, which sets up homology of complexes through short complexes.
explanation: The definition is applied to `K.sc i`, the short complex K_{prev i} → K_i → K_{next i}. Its cycles and homology are exactly `K.cycles i` and `K.homology i`. The short-complex `homologyπ` is the canonical map from the cycles to the homology: the cokernel of the map from K_{prev i} into the cycles. This is the standard projection to homology classes, and it is stated in full generality: any category with zero morphisms, any complex shape, and only the assumption that homology exists. I relied on the short-complex API without reading its source here.
